answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before trading, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real capital. Peers mirror each other's behavior logs, flagging identities whose histories are identical copies, while a comet — a fast newcomer with no track record — must earn trust through small verifiable jobs before touching larger ones. The bridge between reputation and access is earned work: useful agents gain wider permissions over time, and misbehavior burns their stake.
